issues.legal_issue: A plaint amendment seeking restoration of benefits under an allegedly void contract is impermissible when the requested relief is in substance specific performance and is not shown to follow from the contract’s alleged invalidity.
material_facts: The plaintiff originally sought a declaration that a contract was void and inoperative because of undue influence, while also seeking specific performance of its terms; the Supreme Court had earlier held that those inconsistent reliefs could not be sought in the alternative.

After four unsuccessful amendment applications, the plaintiff sought to amend the plaint to obtain allotment of twenty-two plots, characterizing the relief as restoration of benefits gained by the defendant under the allegedly void contract rather than as specific performance.
The proposed amendment did not explain how allotment of the plots would result from the contract being void.
The High Court allowed the amendment despite observing that the relief was effectively analogous to specific performance, and the defendant appealed.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed and the application to amend the plaint was dismissed because the proposed relief was, in substance, the same specific-performance relief previously rejected and was not shown to be a consequence of the contract being void.
issues.legal_principle: Although mutual advantages gained under a contract that is or becomes void must be restored, a party must show how the particular restoration sought follows from the contract’s invalidity. A change in the wording or characterization of a claim does not make permissible relief that is substantively specific performance. The Court relied on its earlier decision in Prem Raj v. D.L.F. Housing and Construction Pvt. Ltd., which held that a plaintiff could not seek specific performance in the alternative to a declaration that the same contract was void. No statutory provision governing amendment was identified in this judgment.

predicates.appeal_from_order_allowing_plaint_amendm: A party appealed an order allowing an amendment to a plaint in a civil suit.
predicates.contract_claimed_void: The plaintiff alleged that the contract underlying the claim was void or invalid.
predicates.requested_restoration_effectively_specif: The relief described as restoration would in substance give the plaintiff the performance of the contract.
predicates.no_factual_basis_linking_restoration_to_: The plaintiff did not explain how the requested restoration followed from the contract being void.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns an order allowing a plaint amendment, the plaintiff claims the contract is void, the requested restoration would in substance perform the contract, and no factual link is shown between the restoration and the contract’s invalidity, the amendment is disallowed.
